sources.entry: Technitium DNS Server - Authoritative/recursive DNS server with ad blocking functionality. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/C#
Technitium DNS Server | Authoritative and recursive DNS server with ad blocking and a web console

summary.one_liner: Technitium DNS Server is an open source authoritative and recursive DNS server with a web console, ad and malware blocking via block lists, and encrypted DNS forwarding.
summary.what_it_does: The server runs on Windows, Linux, macOS and Raspberry Pi, and is also available as a Docker image on Docker Hub. It can act as an authoritative DNS server for your own domains and as a recursive resolver for your network, with block lists used to block ads and malware at the DNS level. Upstream forwarders can use DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-HTTPS, or DNS-over-QUIC, and the server can itself host those encrypted DNS services. It includes caching features (serve stale, prefetch, persistent cache), DNSSEC validation and signing, zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR, NOTIFY), dynamic DNS updates, and a built-in DHCP server. A web console, HTTP API, clustering across multiple instances, OIDC SSO, LDAP, and TOTP 2FA are also described. The software is written in C# on .NET 10.
use_cases: Block ads and malware across a home or office network
Run a private recursive DNS resolver on a home server or Raspberry Pi
Host authoritative DNS for your own domain names
Route DNS queries through encrypted DoT, DoH, or DoQ upstreams
Manage several DNS servers from one web console
Monitor network DNS queries with logs and stats
how_to_run: Windows: download the setup installer from the project's releases or website
Linux and Raspberry Pi: follow the install instructions from the linked blog post
Cross-platform: download the portable app and run it on a system with .NET 10 installed
Docker: pull the official image from Docker Hub and use the docker-compose.yml example
Build from source: follow the Build Instructions in the project documentation
notable: Authoritative and recursive DNS in one server, with DNS Apps for custom response logic
Clustering to manage two or more instances from a single admin console
Broad DNSSEC support including NSEC3 and DANE TLSA
Works out-of-the-box with zero configuration and an HTTP API for automation
caveats: Requires .NET 10 for the portable and cross-platform install
Some features such as DNS rebinding protection are provided through separate DNS Apps
Donations are requested; the README does not describe paid tiers
